title: Looks for macros that expand metavariables in an unsafe block.
summary: This hides an unsafe block and allows the user of the macro to write unsafe code without an explicit unsafe block at callsite, making it possible to perform unsafe operations in seemingly safe code. Clippy puts this lint in the suspicious group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for #[macro_use] use....
summary: Since the Rust 2018 edition you can import macro’s directly, this is considered idiomatic. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for recursion using the entrypoint.
summary: Apart from special setups (which we could detect following attributes like #![no_std]), recursing into main() seems like an unintuitive anti-pattern we should be able to detect. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Detects patterns like if a > b { a - b } else { b - a } and suggests using a.abs_diff(b).
summary: Using abs_diff is shorter, more readable, and avoids control flow. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Detects if-then-panic! that can be replaced with assert!.
summary: assert! is simpler than if-then-panic!. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for assert! and debug_assert! that consist of only an (in)equality check
summary: assert_{eq,ne}! and debug_assert_{eq,ne}! achieves the same goal, and provides some additional debug information Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: It checks for manual implementations of async functions.
summary: It’s more idiomatic to use the dedicated syntax. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for usage of T::BITS - x.leading_zeros() when x.bit_width() is available.
summary: Manual reimplementations of bit_width increase code complexity for little benefit. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for usage of size_of::<T>() * 8 when T::BITS is available.
summary: Can be written as the shorter T::BITS. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for the manual creation of C strings (a string with a NUL byte at the end), either through one of the CStr constructor functions, or more plainly by calling .as_ptr() on a (byte) string literal with a hardcoded \0 byte at the end.
summary: This can be written more concisely using c"str" literals and is also less error-prone, because the compiler checks for interior NUL bytes and the terminating NUL byte is inserted automatically. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Detects manual zero checks before dividing integers, such as if x != 0 { y / x }.
summary: checked_div already handles the zero case and makes the intent clearer while avoiding a panic from a manual division. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Identifies good opportunities for a clamp function from std or core, and suggests using it.
summary: clamp is much shorter, easier to read, and doesn’t use any control flow. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for .truncate(0) calls on standard library types where it can be replaced with .clear().
summary: clear() expresses the intent better and is likely to be more efficient than truncate(0). Clippy puts this lint in the perf group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for usage of iter().any() on slices when it can be replaced with contains() and suggests doing so.
summary: contains() is more concise and idiomatic, while also being faster in some cases. Clippy puts this lint in the perf group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for casts of small constant literals or mem::align_of results to raw pointers.
summary: This creates a dangling pointer and is better expressed as {std, core}::ptr::{dangling, dangling_mut}. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for an expression like (x + (y - 1)) / y which is a common manual reimplementation of x.div_ceil(y).
summary: It’s simpler, clearer and more readable. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for usage of match which could be implemented using filter
summary: Using the filter method is clearer and more concise. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for usage of _.filter(_).map(_) that can be written more simply as filter_map(_).
summary: Redundant code in the filter and map operations is poor style and less performant. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for manual implementations of Iterator::find
summary: It doesn’t affect performance, but using find is shorter and easier to read. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for usage of _.find(_).map(_) that can be written more simply as find_map(_).
summary: Redundant code in the find and map operations is poor style and less performant. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for unnecessary if let usage in a for loop where only the Some or Ok variant of the iterator element is used.
summary: It is verbose and can be simplified by first calling the flatten method on the Iterator. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for cases where BuildHasher::hash_one can be used.
summary: It is more concise to use the hash_one method. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for manual case-insensitive ASCII comparison.
summary: The eq_ignore_ascii_case method is faster because it does not allocate memory for the new strings, and it is more readable. Clippy puts this lint in the perf group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for expressions like N - x.leading_zeros() (where N is one less than bit width of x) or x.ilog(2), which are manual reimplementations of x.ilog2()
summary: Manual reimplementations of ilog2 increase code complexity for little benefit. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for uses of map which return the original item.
summary: inspect is both clearer in intent and shorter. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Lints subtraction between Instant::now() and another Instant.
summary: It is easy to accidentally write prev_instant - Instant::now(), which will always be 0ns as Instant subtraction saturates. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Suggests to use dedicated built-in methods, is_ascii_(lowercase|uppercase|digit|hexdigit) for checking on corresponding ascii range
summary: Using the built-in functions is more readable and makes it clear that it’s not a specific subset of characters, but all ASCII (lowercase|uppercase|digit|hexdigit) characters. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for manual is_finite reimplementations (i.e., x != <float>::INFINITY && x != <float>::NEG_INFINITY).
summary: The method is_finite is shorter and more readable. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for manual is_infinite reimplementations (i.e., x == <float>::INFINITY || x == <float>::NEG_INFINITY).
summary: The method is_infinite is shorter and more readable. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for manual implementation of .is_multiple_of() on unsigned integer types.
summary: a.is_multiple_of(b) is a clearer way to check for divisibility of a by b. This expression can never panic. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for expressions like x.count_ones() == 1 or x & (x - 1) == 0, with x and unsigned integer, which may be manual reimplementations of x.is_power_of_two().
summary: Manual reimplementations of is_power_of_two increase code complexity for little benefit. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for usage of option.map(f).unwrap_or_default() and result.map(f).unwrap_or_default() where f is a function or closure that returns the bool type.
summary: Readability. These can be written more concisely as option.is_some_and(f) and result.is_ok_and(f). Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for manual implementations of isolating the lowest set bit.
summary: The manual bit-twiddling forms are harder to read than the standard library method. Using -x can also overflow for signed minimum values. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Warn of cases where let...else could be used
summary: let...else provides a standard construct for this pattern that people can easily recognize. It’s also more compact. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for references on std::path::MAIN_SEPARATOR.to_string() used to build a &str.
summary: There exists a std::path::MAIN_SEPARATOR_STR which does not require an extra memory allocation. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for usage of match which could be implemented using map
summary: Using the map method is clearer and more concise. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for for-loops that manually copy items between slices that could be optimized by having a memcpy.
summary: It is not as fast as a memcpy. Clippy puts this lint in the perf group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for manual implementation of midpoint.
summary: Using (x + y) / 2 or (x + y) >> 1 on integer types might cause an overflow on the intermediate addition result. The latter will only warn for unsigned integer types. Similar for floating-point (x + y) / 2.0 and (x + y) * 0.5. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for .rev().next() on a DoubleEndedIterator
summary: .next_back() is cleaner. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for manual implementations of the non-exhaustive pattern.
summary: Using the #[non_exhaustive] attribute expresses better the intent and allows possible optimizations when applied to enums. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for manual implementations of std::task::Wake that are empty.
summary: Waker::noop() provides a more performant and cleaner way to create a waker that does nothing, avoiding unnecessary Arc allocations and reference count increments. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for manual implementation of .ok() or .err() on Result values.
summary: Using .ok() or .err() rather than a match or if let is less complex and more readable. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Finds patterns that reimplement Option::ok_or.
summary: Concise code helps focusing on behavior instead of boilerplate. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: This detects various manual reimplementations of Option::as_slice.
summary: Those implementations are both more complex than calling as_slice and unlike that incur a branch, pessimizing performance and leading to more generated code. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for usage of a.and_then(|a| b.map(|b| (a, b))) which can be more concisely expressed as a.zip(b).
summary: Option::zip is more concise and directly expresses the intent of combining two Option values into a tuple. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for manual char comparison in string patterns
summary: This can be written more concisely using a char or an array of char. This is more readable and more optimized when comparing to only one char. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for code to be replaced by pop_if methods.
summary: Using pop_if is more concise and idiomatic. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for expressions like x >= 3 && x < 8 that could be more readably expressed as (3..8).contains(&x).
summary: contains expresses the intent better and has less failure modes (such as fencepost errors or using || instead of &&). Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Looks for combined OR patterns that are all contained in a specific range, e.g. 6 | 4 | 5 | 9 | 7 | 8 can be rewritten as 4..=9.
summary: Using an explicit range is more concise and easier to read. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for an expression like ((x % 4) + 4) % 4 which is a common manual reimplementation of x.rem_euclid(4).
summary: It’s simpler and more readable. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for repeat().take() that can be replaced with repeat_n().
summary: Using repeat_n() is more concise and clearer. Also, repeat_n() is sometimes faster than repeat().take() when the type of the element is non-trivial to clone because the original value can be reused for the last .next() call rather than always cloning. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for code to be replaced by .retain().
summary: .retain() is simpler and avoids needless allocation. Clippy puts this lint in the perf group, at the level warn.

title: It detects manual bit rotations that could be rewritten using standard functions rotate_left or rotate_right.
summary: Calling the function better conveys the intent. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for .checked_add/sub(x).unwrap_or(MAX/MIN).
summary: These can be written simply with saturating_add/sub methods. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for manually filling a slice with a value.
summary: Using the fill method is more idiomatic and concise. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: When a is &[T], detect a.len() * size_of::<T>() and suggest size_of_val(a) instead.
summary: Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for usage of str::splitn(2, _)
summary: split_once is both clearer in intent and slightly more efficient. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for manual implementations of str::repeat
summary: These are both harder to read, as well as less performant. Clippy puts this lint in the perf group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for usage of "" to create a String, such as "".to_string(), "".to_owned(), String::from("") and others.
summary: Different ways of creating an empty string makes your code less standardized, which can be confusing. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Suggests using strip_{prefix,suffix} over str::{starts,ends}_with and slicing using the pattern’s length.
summary: Using str:strip_{prefix,suffix} is safer and may have better performance as there is no slicing which may panic and the compiler does not need to insert this panic code. It is also sometimes more readable as it removes the need for duplicating or storing the pattern used by str::{starts,ends}_with and in the slicing. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for manual swapping.
summary: The std::mem::swap function exposes the intent better without deinitializing or copying either variable. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Detects manual re-implementations of std::mem::take.
summary: Because the function call is shorter and easier to read. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for usage of Iterator::fold with a type that implements Try.
summary: The code should use try_fold instead, which short-circuits on failure, thus opening the door for additional optimizations not possible with fold as rustc can guarantee the function is never called on None, Err, etc., alleviating otherwise necessary checks. It’s also slightly more idiomatic. Clippy puts this lint in the perf group, at the level warn.

title: Finds patterns that reimplement Option::unwrap_or or Result::unwrap_or.
summary: Concise code helps focusing on behavior instead of boilerplate. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks if a match or if let expression can be simplified using .unwrap_or_default().
summary: It can be done in one call with .unwrap_or_default(). Clippy puts this lint in the suspicious group, at the level warn.

title: Looks for loops that check for emptiness of a Vec in the condition and pop an element in the body as a separate operation.
summary: Such loops can be written in a more idiomatic way by using a while-let loop and directly pattern matching on the return value of Vec::pop(). Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for too many variables whose name consists of a single character.
summary: It’s hard to memorize what a variable means without a descriptive name. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for usage of .map(…), followed by .all(identity) or .any(identity).
summary: The .all(…) or .any(…) methods can be called directly in place of .map(…). Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for usage of map(|x| x.clone()) or dereferencing closures for Copy types, on Iterator or Option, and suggests cloned() or copied() instead
summary: Readability, this can be written more concisely Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for usage of _.map(_).collect::<Result<(), _>().
summary: Using try_for_each instead is more readable and idiomatic. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for usage of contains_key + insert on HashMap or BTreeMap.
summary: Using entry is more efficient. Clippy puts this lint in the perf group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for instances of map_err(|_| Some::Enum)
summary: This map_err throws away the original error rather than allowing the enum to contain and report the cause of the error. Clippy puts this lint in the restriction group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for usage of _.map(_).flatten(_) on Iterator, Option, and Result.
summary: Readability. This can be written more concisely with Iterator::flat_map, Option::and_then, and Result::and_then. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for instances of map(f) where f is the identity function.
summary: It can be written more concisely without the call to map. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks the usage of .map_or(...) with an identity function for Option and Result types.
summary: This can be written more concisely by using unwrap_or(). Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for usage of option.map(_).unwrap_or(_) or option.map(_).unwrap_or_else(_) or result.map(_).unwrap_or_else(_).
summary: Readability, these can be written more concisely (resp.) as option.map_or(_, _), option.map_or_else(_, _) and result.map_or_else(_, _). Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for Iterator::map over ranges without using the parameter which could be more clearly expressed using std::iter::repeat(...).take(...) or std::iter::repeat_n.
summary: It expresses the intent more clearly to take the correct number of times from a generating function than to apply a closure to each number in a range only to discard them. Clippy puts this lint in the restriction group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for match which is used to add a reference to an Option value.
summary: Using as_ref() or as_mut() instead is shorter. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for matches where match expression is a bool.
summary: It suggests to replace the expression with an if...else block. It makes the code less readable. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for match or if let expressions producing a bool that could be written using matches!
summary: Readability and needless complexity. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Nothing.
summary: This lint has been deprecated Clippy puts this lint in the deprecated group, at the level none.

title: Checks for overlapping match arms.
summary: It is likely to be an error and if not, makes the code less obvious. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for matches where all arms match a reference, suggesting to remove the reference and deref the matched expression instead.
summary: It also checks for if let &foo = bar blocks. It just makes the code less readable. That reference destructuring adds nothing to the code. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for unnecessary ok() in while let.
summary: Calling ok() in while let is unnecessary, instead match on Ok(pat) Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for match with identical arm bodies.
summary: This is probably a copy & paste error. If arm bodies are the same on purpose, you can factor them using |. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for useless match that binds to only one value.
summary: Readability and needless complexity. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for match expressions modifying the case of a string with non-compliant arms
summary: The arm is unreachable, which is likely a mistake Clippy puts this lint in the correctness group, at the level deny.

title: Checks for arm which matches all errors with Err(_) and take drastic actions like panic!.
summary: It is generally a bad practice, similar to catching all exceptions in java with catch(Exception) Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for wildcard enum matches for a single variant.
summary: New enum variants added by library updates can be missed. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for iteration that may be infinite.
summary: While there may be places where this is acceptable (e.g., in event streams), in most cases this is simply an error. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.
